canonical_data: SQLite/Postgres-backed append-only conversation event log (UUIDv7-ordered) plus committed prompt/config files, artifacts, and sandbox snapshot references
strengths: A clean exoharness/executor split keeps durable state, sandbox lifecycle, and secrets in an immutable, event-sourced substrate while agent semantics (prompts, tools, compaction, model choice) stay fully swappable and self-editable
Named executor presets let a turn be delegated to Codex, Claude Code, Cursor, or Pi running inside the managed sandbox, alongside first-class OpenAI, Anthropic, and OpenRouter model bindings
A durable append-only event log, live event streaming, and per-service logs give strong visibility into a self-modifying agent's history, with sandbox snapshot/rewind for backing out of bad changes
weaknesses: No GitHub releases or tags exist; the project ships directly off main at a fixed 0.1.0, and the README calls it early-stage, with self-maintenance, recoverable execution, and full clone/lineage-based multi-agent orchestration listed as unbuilt roadmap items

Recursive self-modification of harness policy, tools, and prompts is bounded only by an immutable event log as a policy choice; no documented human approval gate exists before the agent rebuilds and restarts its own runtime
Sandbox snapshot and rewind do not yet work across process restarts, and generalized computer-use of windowed GUIs is an acknowledged gap
why_it_matters: One of the few open harnesses built explicitly around recursive self-modification: it isolates an immutable event log and sandbox substrate from fully agent-editable semantics, letting future models safely evolve every layer of their own runtime rather than only their memory.
